title: Reduction for a Resort Lodging Reservation Recorded Well Before Arrival
content:
How far ahead a Resort Lodging reservation was recorded decides the advance booking reduction taken on the room rate. The period is counted in calendar days between the day the reservation was recorded and the arrival date carried on it.

Where the reservation was recorded at least twice the unit type's advance period in calendar days before the arrival date, the early booking reduction of 20 percent is taken.

Where the reservation was recorded at least the unit type's advance period but less than twice that period in calendar days before the arrival date, the unit type's advance booking reduction is taken.

Where the reservation was recorded less than the unit type's advance period in calendar days before the arrival date, no advance booking reduction is taken.

## The advance period of each unit type, and twice it

| Unit type | Advance period (calendar days) | Twice the advance period (calendar days) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base Village Inn Room | 60 | 120 |
| Slopeside Studio | 60 | 120 |
| Slopeside One-Bedroom Residence | 90 | 180 |
| Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence | 90 | 180 |
| Mountain Lodge Suite | 90 | 180 |
| Summit Penthouse Residence | 120 | 240 |
| Private Mountain Chalet | 150 | 300 |

### Both sides of each threshold, on a Slopeside Studio (hypothetical bookings)

The unit type's advance period is 60 calendar days and twice it is 120. A reservation recorded 120 calendar days before the arrival date reaches twice the period, so the early booking reduction of 20 percent is taken. A reservation recorded 119 calendar days before arrival falls short of twice the period but reaches the period itself, so the unit type's advance booking reduction is taken instead. A reservation recorded 60 calendar days before arrival still reaches the period and takes the same middle tier. A reservation recorded 59 calendar days before arrival falls short of the period, and no advance booking reduction is taken.
